resolvedQuestions.text: How should goal.md enter the Level contract (optionalAddonDocs vs lazyAddonDocs), which levels, and what should the template contain for phase-parent vs child?
How do Claude Code native goal and the local opencode-goal plugin differ, and what does the missing Claude adapter imply?
Should the speckit goal_prompting / goal_prompt_choice contract become runtime-neutral, and how, given opencode_goal has no Claude adapter?
What wording, parent/child precedence, and validation make a parent-to-child goal.md reference reliable without a dereference mechanism?
Can the acceptance-criteria closure gate serve as the packet-level self-contained stop check given stop-evaluator asymmetry?
How should goal.md split durable directive vs volatile log, and should a validator enforce a parent size cap, given packet 033 drift?

keyFindings.text: goal.md belongs on lazyAddonDocs at levels 1, 2, 3, 3+ and phase-parent; omit review.
In-repo goal surfaces are OpenCode plugin, sibling core (Pi/Cursor), and a Claude hole. 4000-char caps are real. Claude Stop-hook internals are not proven here.
goal_prompting should become runtime-neutral via a dispatch table. Offer already does not call opencode_goal; set is the Claude/Cursor gap.
Parent-to-child references are a prompt convention plus a present-file packet validator. The set string is a short pointer plus copied completion criteria.
AC_CLOSURE is the L2+ packet-close complement, not the session stop evaluator, and it does not run on phase-parent.
Cap the durable slice of parent goal.md at 2000 characters. Do not cap the whole file. 033 goal.md is 15028 bytes with three phases.
